title: Projects
text:
My current research focuses on population health data, healthcare databases, and epidemiological approaches. I am particularly interested in examining complex health challenges through applied research methods and secondary data analysis. My aim is to identify patterns in health outcomes and population-level trends to contribute to evidence-informed public health practice.
Selected research projects are ongoing, and additional details and findings will be shared as the projects progress.

title: Projects
section: School Health Surveillance and Youth Health Data
text:
School Health Surveillance and Youth Health Data

Overview
I’m currently conducting a retrospective, multidomain analysis using existing National and Cuyahoga County Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS).


Aim

To examine if local data on youth health behavior and experiences meaningfully differ from 2023 to 2025.
To identify potential demographic disparities and whether existing gaps changed between the 2023 and 2025 county-level surveys
To evaluate if the 2026 WWISS-CC youth interns’ need assessment aligns with priority areas revealed from 2023 and 2025 Cuyahoga County YRBS data

title: Projects
section: Youth Data Literacy and Public Health Curriculum Development
text:
Youth Data Literacy and Public Health Curriculum Development

Overview
I’m in the process of creating a formal guide to be used for future WWISS-CC youth internship programs.


Aim
The goal of this curriculum guide is to provide a structured, seven-week program to promote high school interns learning about data, public health surveillance, and school health.
The curriculum will contain background of the WWISS-CC initative, learning objectives, a seven-week lesson plan, facilitation guides, activity instructions, and evaluations.


Methods

Literature review conducted to find information on youth data literacy and youth-led participatory action research (YPAR) to create an evidence-based foundation for the curriculum lesson plans.
Utilizing a 5E Instructional Model (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate) to teach youth about data literacy while making the process to be interactive.

title: Projects
section: Secondary Analysis of Healthcare Utilization Among Medicare Beneficiaries with Diagnosed Depression: A Comparison Across Chronic Conditions
text:
Secondary Analysis of Healthcare Utilization Among Medicare Beneficiaries with Diagnosed Depression: A Comparison Across Chronic Conditions

Overview
This is a semester-long project for the Secondary Analysis of Large Healthcare Databases (PQHS 515) course I’m enrolled in. This is an observational study using secondary data from the publicly available CMS Linkable 2008-2010 Medicare Data Entrepreneurs’ Synthetic Public Use File (DE-SynPUF) to examine the association between hospitalization rates and diagnosed depression among Medicare beneficiaries with at least one of the five listed chronic conditions: diabetes, ischemic heart disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and Alzheimer’s disease or related disorders.


Aim
The objective of this study is to identify the highest hospitalization percentages among the depression-chronic condition combinations, as well to investigate whether depression was associated with hospitalization within each of selected chronic condition groups.

Welcome to my website!
My name is Eliza Brinton, and I’m currently a second-year Masters of Public Health student at Case Western Reserve University studying population health research.
Currently, my research is focused on the utilization of youth data and surveillance to help drive evidence-based policies and programs for school districts throughout Cuyahoga County. Additionally, my work uses data-driven approaches to monitor youth health trends and risk behaviors to support and improve adolescent health and well-being.
Thank you for visiting my website! Here, you can find my CV and contact information, as well as updates on my current research projects.”
Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions or would like to discuss potential projects.

title: Photography
text:
As a wizard and scholar of Middle-earth, I have been studying the magic of the natural world for centuries. Through my self-portraits, I aim to capture the essence of my own being and reflect on my own journey through time. Each photograph is a reflection of my own experiences and emotions. Through my photography, I hope to offer a glimpse into my life as a scholar and adventurer, and inspire others to reflect on their own journeys through the world.
